exposure: Intrathecal bupivacaine with fentanyl 25 mg and morphine 100 mg
cohort: The study included 60 parturients scheduled for elective caesarean section.
finding: The intrathecal combination of fentanyl and morphine provided better intraoperative analgesia, requiring less additional analgesia, compared to morphine alone, but led to higher rates of postoperative nausea and vomiting and increased pethidine consumption in the first 12 postoperative hours.
mod_finding: Intrathecal fentanyl combined with morphine may offer improved perioperative analgesia for caesarean section, particularly when the time from anesthesia to skin incision is short.
